Noturus miurus Jordan, 1877. Size: 130 mm (5.1") SL. Type locality: White River, near Indianapolis, Marion County, Indiana, U.S.A.

Identification: light yellow or brown above with dark mottling; 4 vague saddles; white to yellow below; brown or black border on the caudal fin; brown or black mottling on the other fins. Head rounded above.

North America: lower Great Lakes drainages in Ontario, Canada and New York, USA, southwest through most of the Ohio River basin and lower Mississippi River basin (west to eastern Kansas and Oklahoma); Mohawk River in New York; Pearl River and Lake Pontchartrain drainages in Mississippi and Louisiana, USA.
Inhabits riffles, pools below riffles and runs over gravel and sand mixed with sticks and leaves in creeks and small rivers. Also found in lakes.
Provide sand mixed with peat moss, PVC pipes, flat rocks and vegetation.
Readily feeds on live and frozen foods. Will also adapt to flake and prepared foods for the aquarium.
Suitable for a coldwater community tank. Ideal tank mates include small to midsized North American native fishes such as darters and shiners.
Breeding male with swollen lips, enlarged cephalic epaxial muscles, and large bulbous genital papilla. Female with papilla with deep median groove ending in a small bump.

Spawning occurs in the months of May-August. It is difficult in the aquarium, however it has been done when wild caught specimens are added to aquariums with warmer temperatures than the river or drainage system they are captured from.
Etymology: from the Greek notos, meaning back, and oura, meaning tail, in reference to the confluent adipose and caudal fins. The specific epithet refers to the stout appearance of some specimens.
Annals of the Lyceum of Natural History of New York v. 11 (nos 11-12) (art. 29), pp 371.
